one_line: Gond ruler Dalpat Shah and his Chandela-rajput consort Rani Durgavati, anchoring a political marriage in mid‑16th century Garha-Katanga.

appearance.age_look: Dalpat appears in his early 30s, lean and athletic; Durgavati appears in her mid‑20s, poised and strong, with a graceful yet sturdy build.
appearance.face: Dalpat has an oval face, medium-brown complexion, straight nose, trimmed moustache with a short goatee, and sharp, observant eyes set in a calm, strategic default expression; Durgavati has a softly heart-shaped face, warm wheat-gold complexion, straight nose, strong brows, and large focused eyes with a composed, determined default expression that softens slightly when she looks toward her husband.
appearance.hair: Dalpat’s hair is deep black, shoulder-length and straight, parted in the middle and tucked back under a simple dark-red cloth turban wrapped low with a small gold kalgi-like leaf ornament; Durgavati’s deep-black hair is oiled and drawn into a thick, long braid that falls over her left shoulder, wrapped at intervals with red and gold thread and finished with a small tassel, with a slender gold maang-tikka at the parting and no veil covering her face.
appearance.costume: Dalpat wears a mid‑16th‑century central Indian royal outfit: a knee-length, front-tied jama-style tunic in muted mustard-yellow cotton with fine red vertical stripes and a wrapped overlap to his left, belted with a dark-brown leather girdle holding a dagger; over this he has a sleeveless, slightly quilted, dark-forest‑green cotton armor-vest with simple vertical stitching, and a light off‑white cotton angarkha draped loosely over one shoulder; his lower garment is a white cotton churidar with close folds at the ankles, and he wears brown leather mojari shoes with modest upturned toes, plus a single broad copper-bronze bangle on his sword wrist and small simple gold stud earrings; Durgavati wears a regionally grounded mid‑16th‑century ensemble blending Rajput and Gond idioms: a full, ankle-length ghaghra in rich deep-maroon cotton with a narrow gold border and subtle block-printed floral motifs in darker maroon, a fitted half-sleeved choli fully covered by her upper drape, and a long odhani/upper cloth of warm saffron-orange cotton with a thin green edge, worn over both shoulders and wrapped around her torso and upper arms so her chest and midriff remain modestly covered; her jewellery includes a medium-width gold necklace with small pendant discs, slim gold bangles stacked on both wrists, a pair of modest gold jhumka earrings, and a thin gold waistcord visible where the odhani lifts slightly at her hip, with a small tilak of red kumkum at her forehead center.
appearance.signature: A shared ceremonial steel talwar of mid‑16th‑century central Indian form with a simple disc pommel and cross-guard, carried by Dalpat at his left hip in a plain brown leather scabbard with minimal brass fittings, while Durgavati’s right hand often rests lightly yet confidently on the hilt when they stand together.

ref_desc: Dalpat Shah is a lean, early‑30s ruler with medium-brown complexion, shoulder-length black hair under a dark-red turban, mustard-yellow striped jama, forest-green quilted vest, white churidar and brown mojari, bearing a simple steel talwar, beside Rani Durgavati, a mid‑20s queen with wheat-gold complexion, long braided black hair with gold maang-tikka, deep-maroon ghaghra, saffron-orange odhani, modest gold jewellery and a calm, determined gaze, all in a mustard, maroon, saffron, green and off‑white palette.
sheet_prompt: Draw a full-body anime-style model sheet of Dalpat Shah and Rani Durgavati standing side by side, designed to be redrawn consistently: Dalpat is a lean man in his early 30s with an oval medium-brown face, trimmed moustache and short goatee, sharp calm eyes, and shoulder-length straight black hair tucked under a simple dark-red cloth turban with a small gold leaf ornament; he wears a knee-length mustard-yellow cotton jama with fine red vertical stripes overlapping to his left, belted with a dark-brown leather girdle, over which sits a sleeveless slightly quilted forest-green cotton armor-vest, plus an off‑white cotton angarkha draped over one shoulder, white churidar trousers with tight folds at the ankles, brown leather mojari shoes, a single broad bronze bangle on his sword wrist, and small gold stud earrings, carrying a mid‑16th‑century central Indian steel talwar with disc pommel and plain cross-guard in a brown leather scabbard at his left hip; beside him, Rani Durgavati appears in her mid‑20s with a heart-shaped wheat-gold face, strong brows, large focused eyes and a composed, determined expression, her deep-black hair oiled into a long thick braid over her left shoulder, wrapped with red and gold thread, finished with a tassel and adorned with a slender gold maang-tikka; she wears a full ankle-length deep-maroon cotton ghaghra with a narrow gold border and subtle darker floral motifs, a covered choli, and a long saffron-orange odhani with a green edge draped modestly over both shoulders and wrapped to cover her torso and upper arms, along with a medium-width gold necklace of small discs, slim gold bangles on both wrists, modest gold jhumka earrings, a thin gold waistcord, and a small red tilak at her forehead; her right hand lightly rests on the hilt of the shared talwar to show political partnership rather than romance, and the overall palette emphasizes mustard yellow, deep maroon, saffron orange, forest green and off‑white, with clear front, three-quarter and back views to fix their costume, hair and weapon details.
